title: Tennis Australia Strengthens Child Safety Across Queensland Clubs
body: Tennis Queensland has introduced updated child safety measures across its community club network. All affiliated clubs are now required to implement strengthened child safe policies and procedures in line with national standards. Tennis Australia has released supporting resources to help clubs meet these requirements.

title: Second Victorian Sporting Club Under Fire for Safeguarding Breach
body: A second sporting club in Victoria's south-west has been criticised for allowing a convicted child sex offender to participate in community sport. The incident has prompted renewed calls for stronger verification processes and more rigorous compliance with Working With Children Check requirements across community clubs.

title: NSW Suspends Two Early Learning Services Over Child Safety Concerns
body: The NSW Department of Education has suspended two early learning services following significant child safety concerns. While this action relates to early childhood education rather than sport, it demonstrates the regulatory approach being applied across child-focused sectors in NSW. Sporting organisations should note the increasing regulatory scrutiny on child safe practices.

title: Melbourne Transport Incident Highlights Child Safety Protocol Importance
body: A child safety incident involving a Melbourne bus has prompted review of safety protocols for transporting children. While not sport-specific, the incident serves as a reminder for sporting clubs about the importance of robust procedures when transporting young participants to and from training and events.
